churn_resistance.rationale: The architecture is built to survive churn: one data-access module, typed API boundary, single-point runtime config, and config files identical to fresh v22 CLI output. Docked for the effect-as-state-propagation workaround, the DOM-bypassing scroll hack, and 7-way title duplication that a future refactor would have to sweep up.

findings.issue: An effect copies `resource.value()` into a `view` signal to keep the previous list visible during reload — state propagation via effect, which Angular's own guidance flags as the wrong tool and a source of timing bugs.
findings.suggestion: Use `resource({defaultValue: …})` / `linkedSignal`, or simply render from the resource and accept the loading state like the other six pages do.

findings.issue: Search input has no debounce: every keystroke triggers `router.navigate` plus a resource reload that can fan out up to 48 parallel Pokémon requests; the loader also ignores the resource's `abortSignal`.
findings.suggestion: Debounce the search by up to 300 ms (explicitly allowed by the spec) before navigating, and abort in-flight loads when params change.

findings.issue: The `#moves` anchor jump is hand-rolled with `effect` + `setTimeout` + `window.location.hash` + `document.getElementById`, a fragile timing hack that bypasses the Router and runs before the DOM is updated.
findings.suggestion: Use `afterRenderEffect` (the current API for post-render DOM work) or enable `withInMemoryScrolling({anchorScrolling: 'enabled'})` on the Router, keeping the hash handling inside the framework.

findings.issue: The `<title> – Pokédex` rule is re-implemented in 7 components.
findings.suggestion: Add `title` route data plus a small custom `TitleStrategy` so the suffix lives in one place and future pages inherit it.

findings.issue: `provideHttpClient(withFetch())` is redundant in Angular v22, where HttpClient uses the fetch backend and needs no providers at all.
findings.suggestion: Drop the provider entirely (only add `provideHttpClient(...)` when configuring interceptors/XSRF), so future majors never have to migrate this line.

findings.issue: `@angular/forms` is a declared dependency but is never imported; the app uses plain native form elements.
The `moveTables` loader reads `this.base.value()!` — a non-null assertion coupling two resources; if `base` reloads between the `params` check and the loader body, this throws.
findings.suggestion: Pass the Pokémon's moves (or the base resource identity) through `params` so the loader only runs on stable inputs, or merge the two loads into one resource.

findings.issue: Zero unit tests despite `ng test` being wired up (v22 defaults to Vitest); all safety nets are external Playwright acceptance tests.
findings.suggestion: Add Vitest specs for the pure helpers (helpers.ts) and the filter/sort logic, which are exactly the parts most likely to churn silently.

findings.issue: CSR-only rendering means unknown resources can never return HTTP 404 (spec says it's encouraged where the architecture allows).
findings.suggestion: Given the constraints (browser-reachable API, single static server) CSR is defensible; if 404 status ever matters, Angular's stable route-level render mode (SSR) would slot into the existing server.mjs with a per-route prerender exclusion.

summary: This is a current-generation Angular 22 app: new-in-v22 `Service()` and stable `resource()`, signal inputs, @let, zoneless/OnPush defaults and lazy routes, with all API access and display rules funneled through two core services — it would take an Angular 23 upgrade with almost no code churn. The genuine forward-thinking misses are local, not architectural: a signal-writing effect used as a state-propagation workaround, an effect/setTimeout scroll hack instead of `afterRenderEffect` or router anchor scrolling, an undebounced search, and a duplicated title rule across seven components. Dependencies are lean and current except an unused `@angular/forms`.

apis.replacement: In v22 HttpClient is fetch-backed and injectable with no providers; the call is redundant but not deprecated
Allowed but discouraged for state propagation — use computed()/linkedSignal()/resource defaultValue; for DOM work use afterRenderEffect
Prefer route `title` + custom TitleStrategy to centralize the '– Pokédex' suffix
